One membership. Zero juggling.

Your week, minus the seventeen tabs.

Right now your Saturday is a soft play booking in one app, a gym class in another, a babysitter on WhatsApp and a cold coffee in the car between Chesham, Amersham and Berkhamsted.

The Bury puts everything inside one gate. Drop the kids at the crash gym or crèche, take a class or clear your inbox in a panelled study, then all meet for lunch by the lake. One subscription. One estate. Your village, rebuilt — in a house that's been here three hundred years.

The Opportunity — for investors & partners

London proved the model. The Bury is the venue London can't have.

Family members' clubs are one of hospitality's fastest-validating categories: OurHouse's London clubs sold out initial memberships within minutes and took £100m from Blackstone to expand. No comparable club exists in the Chilterns commuter belt — home to exactly the families who priced those London clubs out in the first place. And where London operators retrofit urban buildings, The Bury offers what they can't: a 1712 estate with 4.7 acres and a lake, half a mile from a Metropolitan line station.

£100m

Blackstone's investment into OurHouse to roll out three more London family clubs — institutional validation of the category.

Minutes

How long initial membership allocations took to sell out at OurHouse's London sites, with rolling waitlists since 2022.

0

Comparable family clubs serving Chesham, Amersham, Berkhamsted, Beaconsfield and the wider Chilterns belt.

Why The Bury, why now

The towns around it — Amersham, Berkhamsted, Beaconsfield, Gerrards Cross, the Chalfonts — hold one of the densest concentrations of high-income young families in the country: London leavers who traded the city for schools and gardens, and miss having somewhere to go.

The estate is available to let now, in Class E use — the class that already spans workspace, fitness, crèche and café uses, materially reducing planning risk. The listed house takes the quiet uses; the Stables takes the loud ones.

Our wedge is the crash gym: a genuine kid-magnet anchor no London club leads with, driving weekly visit frequency and party revenue from day one.

Illustrative model: blended £300/family/month, ~15% secondary spend, mature-year opex ~£1.05m including estimated full-estate rent (part-lets quoted from £3,313 pcm; whole-estate terms to be agreed). Cash breakeven ≈ 255 families. All assumptions open for diligence.

The ask

Raising a founding round to secure the estate lease, convert the Stables into the crash gym, sensitively fit out the listed house, and open with a waitlist already in hand. Full deck, estate particulars and model available on request.

A note from the founder

I'm building the place I couldn't find. Want to build it with me?

Every weekend I watched Chilterns families do what mine did: drive between a soft play, a gym, a café and a birthday party, spending a fortune to be apart from each other. London parents got a better answer. Ours should be better still — and it comes with a lake.

I'm looking for a cofounder or operating partner — someone with hospitality, fitness or property operating experience who wants to build the family club the Home Counties deserve — and the investors to back the first site.

— Maisie
